question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $9,$ the additive inverse of $27$ modulo $9$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $27$ modulo $9$ is the integer $0\le x<9$ such that

$$
x+27≡0\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

First, note that $27≡3\cdot 9≡0\,(\text{mod}\,9),$ and $0+0≡0\,(\text{mod}\,9).$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $27$ modulo $9$ is $0.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
27+0≡3\cdot 9+0≡3\cdot 0+0≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,9)
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
